title: Project Visibility per Agent Owner
dataSources: Project collaborator lists and roles (owner, editor, annotator, viewer) in the Splunk Agent Observability console
description: Keeps each owner's agents visible only to that owner and to the people they share with, by using one Splunk Agent Observability project per owner and reviewing project collaborators.
value: Agent traces contain prompts, tool results and sometimes customer data. Project boundaries are how Splunk Agent Observability separates them, so reviewing them is the access control for that data.
implementation: Give each owner their own project and share it with that owner. Review collaborators on every project each quarter and remove anyone who no longer needs access. Do not split one application across projects: a second project splits its traces.
visualization: Project collaborator list per project, exported to the access review record.
knownFalsePositives: Admins see every project by design. A lab or workshop tenant often has a single project for everyone; say so rather than creating a second project to demonstrate separation.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

No agent instrumentation change. Point each owner's agents at their own project with `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT`.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

A project is one application and the visibility boundary. By default only the creator and admins see it. System roles on SaaS are `agent_observability_admin`, `agent_observability_manager`, `agent_observability_user` and `agent_observability_read_only`; on-prem they are Admin, Manager, User and Read-only. These are not Splunk Observability Cloud roles. Project collaborators are owner, editor, annotator and viewer, and the API default for a new collaborator is viewer.

Step 3 — Validate

Log in as a test user who is not a collaborator and confirm the project is not visible. Only admin is documented as seeing every project. The documentation disagrees on whether a manager sees every project or only shared ones, so confirm on the tenant before relying on either. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

File the collaborator list with the quarterly access review.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

A user sees a project they were not shared on: check their system role first, since admins see every project.
grandmaExplanation: Each team gets its own locked folder for its assistant's notes, and we regularly check who holds a key.

productArtifacts.title: Quarterly project collaborator review
productArtifacts.body:
Rule: one project per owner; share the project with that owner.
Review: for each project, list collaborators and their role (owner, editor, annotator, viewer).
Default: a collaborator added through the API is a viewer unless set otherwise.
Remove: collaborators who no longer need access.
Do not claim: whether managers see unshared projects; the documentation disagrees.
